extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters learning news genres and techniques
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter showing example articles and implicit production/evaluation criteria across news genres (financial reports, market round-ups, anecdotal features, expedition reporting, etc.) to teach reporters what elements each type should contain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal bond sale reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the sale price, competing bids, composition of the issue, maturities and coupon rates, and tax status; provide interpretive market context and historical comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific numbers (e.g., "The bid of the winning company was 100.567, while the second bid was... 100.44"). Spell out the issue composition and terms (amounts by loan, years, and rates: "Municipal building loan, 20 years, 4 per cent, $200,000; ... Fulton-street loan, 20 years, 4 1/2 per cent, $400,000..."). Note tax treatment ("These bonds are tax exempt, the exemption extending to the federal income tax"), name successful bidders/agents ("The successful bidders, N. W. Harris & Co, are represented in this city by Percy O. Dorr"), and analyze significance (e.g., "The rate at which these bonds were sold shows that the state of the money market is not as far from normal..."). Provide broker/underwriter offered bases for different maturities and compare to past bases to give historical perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railroad / corporate dividend reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: State declared dividend amounts and contrast with usual/historical dividends; give company capitalization figures, the financial effect of the change, operational scope, ownership relationships, and directors' stated reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report declared vs. usual rates ("declared yesterday a semi-annual dividend of 1 per cent as against the usual dividend of 4 per cent"). Provide issued/outstanding capital and annual disbursements ("The issued capital ... is $80,000,000. The annual disbursement has been ... $5,600,000 annually"). Quantify reduction impact ("the reduced amount of dividends is $2,400,000"; "is equal to about 1/4 per cent on the railroad company's stock"). Explain operational/geographic scope and ownership ("operates all the lines ... west of Pittsburgh"; "All the stock ... is owned by the Pennsylvania Railroad company"). Attribute stated causes from directors ("the cut was due 'chiefly to a large decrease in traffic and a material reduction in the revenues of the lines west of Pittsburgh'"). Mention related board decisions by controlled lines when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity price rumor investigation / local vendor sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a price-increase rumor circulates, seek on-the-record local vendor responses, assess regional supply variation, and report whether wholesale and retail prices support the rumor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote local provision dealers and packing houses (e.g., "There is no truth in the report ... is the declaration of local provision dealers"). Note geographic limits of the cause ("the drought is confined only to certain sections of the state of Kansas"). Compare wholesale and retail levels and margins ("While live stock prices are ... the wholesale prices on the average have also decreased and the housewife is getting the benefit of it"). Include vendor denials of profiteering if given and report reasons (heavy expenses, small profits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local market round-up reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a seasonal overview of supply, origins of produce, packaging and freight considerations, wholesale and retail price ranges, quality/variety distinctions, and inventory/storage statistics where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sources and competition ("Current supplies of peaches are coming from widely separated points... Few California peaches... most of the Georgia crop has also been marketed"). Explain freight/packing costs and their price impact ("Freights and packing cost the New Jersey farmer about 50 cents for an ordinary peach basket"). Report wholesale and retail price ranges with units and package types ("By the dozen, good peaches can be bought for 10 to 25 cents... small baskets ... bring 40 to 50 cents"). Distinguish varieties and quality (clingstones vs freestones; sweetness/flavor). Include inventory data when relevant ("Total stocks in local cold storage warehouses ... were 300,191 packages"). List prices across categories (fruits, vegetables, meats, fish, poultry, butter, eggs) with units (per dozen, per peck, per pound, per basket) to give readers a usable market snapshot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include consumer buying advice within market pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, add short practical advice to readers about selecting quality (what to insist upon and what to avoid) tied to the market information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete buying tips drawn from the market context (e.g., "care should be taken to see that the buyer gets what is wanted... Sweetness and flavor should also be insisted upon, while it is always a mistake to buy half-rotten fruit because it is cheap"). Use advice sparingly and directly related to the described varieties and seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal/human-interest short-feature writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft short human-interest pieces with an immediate, scene-setting lead, colorful dialogue, vivid character details, and a concise resolution or punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a striking moment or line ("When a clerk at the desk of Bretton Hall picked up the desk telephone in response to a ring about nine o'clock last Friday evening he caught the words of the operator"). Use direct, attributed speech to create voice and personality (long dialect quotes in the hotel story). Show rather than tell with specific actions (bootblack coming on a run, elevator door flying open). Conclude with the outcome or wry observation (the lanky boy 'netted him "fo' bits."). Maintain brevity and scene focus for this class of piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transit / routine-observation feature (e.g., subway guard anecdote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report character sketches derived from routine civic operations by describing habitual patterns, regular passengers, and the reporter's or subject's personal knowledge of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center on a recurring pattern and the people involved ("He is on here every night, and he goes to sleep as soon as he gets on the train"). Use the subject's explanations and small-detail observations to produce an intimate, believable portrait (naming stations, routes, typical behaviors). Keep the tone conversational and observational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form narrative feature / adventure/treasure-hunt style
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a sustained narrative with historical set-up, evocative description, a chain of incidents, named characters, document-based clues, and a plot hook (rivalries, counterplots) suited for a magazine-style feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ wide-ranging scene-setting and period detail ('It is a fair day in June, Anno Domini 1684...'), embed historical asides and documented artifacts (charts, ship's bell legend), use time jumps with clear markers ("[Stars here indicate hiatus of 220 years.]"), and build suspense via competing parties and plotted confrontations (Mayflower vs. Merlin). Include character backstories, institutional arrangements (Southern Research Company), and evocative prose; be explicit about names, roles, and motivations. This style tolerates more flourish and narrative voice than straight news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedition / relief-mission reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering relief or exploration missions, identify the mission objective, commander, vessel, sponsoring institutions, logistics/supplies, hazards and likely scenarios, and timeline/possible outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the mission purpose and sponsor ("the American Museum of Natural History ... is sending Pickels to find MacMillan"). Profile the captain and vessel briefly ("Capt. Pickels ... standing on the deck of that stanch little vessel"). Explain logistical preparations (two years' supply of food-stuffs on board), route and ice/navigation hazards (Davis Strait, Melville Bay, 'middle ice'), and potential outcomes (reach objective, wintering in ice). Convey uncertainty and risk candidly to set reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precise units, packaging, and inventory metrics in reporting prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Always report commodity prices with clear units (per dozen, per peck, per pound, per basket), specify package types when relevant, and include inventory/storage statistics when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: prices and units throughout ("peaches... by the dozen... small baskets... full baskets sell at 75 cents to $1.25"); inventory figures ("Total stocks ... were 300,191 packages"). Such precision makes the market report actionable and comparable over time and across sources.
